habitat: Broad-snouted caimans inhabit freshwater wetlands across southeastern South America — from southeastern Brazil through Uruguay, Paraguay, and Bolivia, to northern Argentina. They prefer marshes, swamps, slow-moving rivers, lakes, and flooded savannas. They are highly tolerant of cooler temperatures compared to other crocodilians, extending their range further south. During dry seasons, they may aestivate in burrows dug into mud. They readily colonize man-made water bodies including cattle ponds and reservoirs.
diet: Broad-snouted caimans are generalist carnivores, with diet varying by size and age. Juveniles feed on insects, crustaceans, and small fish. Adults consume fish, amphibians, birds, mammals (including capybaras), and other reptiles. Their broad, robust snout is adapted for crushing mollusks and turtles — a specialization distinguishing them from other caimans. They hunt primarily at night, employing ambush tactics at the water's edge.
behavior: Broad-snouted caimans are relatively social for crocodilians, tolerating others at close range during basking. Males maintain territories during breeding season and may engage in aggressive displays and combat. Females construct mound nests of vegetation and soil, laying 30-50 eggs which incubate for 70-90 days. Mothers guard nests and may assist hatchlings to water. Unlike some crocodilians, broad-snouted caimans are not considered aggressive toward humans.
facts: Broad-snouted caimans can reach 2-3.5 meters in length. Their broad, flat snout — wider than other South American crocodilians — is an adaptation for crushing shelled prey. They are darker and more heavily armored than spectacled caimans. The species was heavily hunted for its skin in the mid-20th century, but populations have recovered under protection and managed ranching programs. They are the southernmost-ranging of all caimans.
naming: Caiman names might reflect their broad snout or South American habitat. Consider names like Broadsnout, Congo (for the Congo Basin comparison), Pantanal, Swampy, Marsh, Crusher, Shell, Argentina, Gaucho, or Rio.
